observed: The real HTTP checks all pass, then recommendation correctly rejects the mismatched runtime identities.
cause: The test fake hardcoded 0ac9dcb while CI merge 79a6404 selected release 47a8e415. Both current-main and exact-merge source readbacks show that selected release.
fix: The expected runtime, fake endpoint version and synthetic trial manifest now use the same selected release. Production acceptance and numerical checks are unchanged.

local_validation.method: A disposable Python entrypoint replaces the selected release object before pytest imports the HTTP fixture. Pytest runs in one process (-n 0), so the synthetic runtime identity survives collection; real HTTP, CLI and acceptance code execute unchanged.

qualification: No actual 47a8e415 GPU measurement or model qualification is claimed. The preset inherits the current selected release; old serving/performance evidence must not transfer to a changed runtime.

first_fix_incomplete.cause: The first fix changed the expected runtime but missed the fake /version response, which still named 0ac9dcb. CI caught the remaining mismatch at deployment verification.
first_fix_incomplete.scope: The failed fixture prevented the numerical HTTP probes from running. These are protocol-test failures, not numerical model findings.
